what: Fighter jet crews parachute safely after collision at US air show

clean_source_blocks.text: Four crew members are in stable condition after two fighter jets collided mid-air during a US air show, officials say. All the aircrew safely ejected from US Navy EA18-G jets that were performing an aerial demonstration when they crashed, a US Navy spokesperson told the BBC's US partner CBS News. It is unclear if they were injured. The dramatic incident happened on Sunday, during the second and final day of the Gunfighter Skies air show, 2 miles (3.2km) northwest of Idaho's Mountain Home Air Force Base. A fire erupted and the base was briefly locked down as the rest of the air show was cancelled. An investigation is underway. "The aircrew involved in the incident are in stable condition," Mountain Air Force Base Gunfighters said in statement posted on social media on Sunday.
The crew members are in a stable condition after the jets crashed mid-air during a demonstration.

The Mountain Home Air Force Base said in a social media post that it was locked down following the incident during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show. Responders were on the scene and an investigation was underway. Four crew members safely ejected after two Navy jets collided during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in western Idaho on Sunday. (Steven S Ogden via Storyful) No other information was immediately available, said a person who answered the phone at the 366th Fighter Wing public affairs office. Multiple witnesses reported two planes collided and crashed, and videos posted online showed four parachutes opening in the sky as the aircraft plummet to the ground near the base about 50 miles (80 kilometers) south of Boise.

A show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho was called off on May 17 after two fighter jets collided, the base said in a statement on Facebook. (Steven S Ogden via Storyful) MOUNTAIN HOME, Idaho - Four crew members safely ejected after two Navy jets collided during an air show in Idaho on Sunday, according to an event organizer. Emergency crews responded after the two planes collided during the show at a military base in western Idaho. All four of the crew members from the planes ejected safely, said Kim Sykes, marketing director with Silver Wings of Idaho, which helped to plan the air show. Sykes said the crash occurred off base and she did not see the crash but saw the smoke afterward.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Four crew members are in stable condition after two fighter jets collided mid-air during a US air show, officials say.

All the aircrew safely ejected from US Navy EA18-G jets that were performing an aerial demonstration when they crashed, a US Navy spokesperson told the BBC's US partner CBS News. It is unclear if they were injured.

The dramatic incident happened on Sunday, during the second and final day of the Gunfighter Skies air show, 2 miles (3.2km) northwest of Idaho's Mountain Home Air Force Base.

A fire erupted and the base was briefly locked down as the rest of the air show was cancelled. An investigation is underway.

"The aircrew involved in the incident are in stable condition," Mountain Air Force Base Gunfighters said in statement posted on social media on Sunday.

"Thank you to all our guests for your patience and compassion, which has allowed us to quickly and safely respond to the incident," the statement said.

Cmdr Amelia Umayam told CBS the crew members were being checked by medical personnel.

Umayam said the EA-18G Growlers were assigned to an electronic attack squadron from Washington state. The US  Navy says each of those jets cost about $67m (£50.3m).

Kim Sykes of Silver Wings of Idaho, which helped organise the air show, told a local CBS affiliate that no-one at the military base was hurt.

The Gunfighter Skies air show was last held in 2018, when a glider pilot died in an accident.

The BBC has contacted the air force base and event organiser for comment.

---

[Lähde: New York Post]
Two jets crashed in midair at an air show in Idaho on Sunday — but all four crew members were able to safely eject, according to reports.

The two aircraft were taking part in the Gunfighters Air Show at the Mountain Home Air Force Base, some 50 miles southeast of Boise, when they crashed, KTVB reported.

Pictures from the scene show a huge plume of black smoke pouring into the sky following the crash, which happened on the second day of the air show.

“We had four good parachutes. The crews were able to eject,” an air show announcer told the crowd, according to the Idaho Statesman.

“They’re located one mile south of where the smoke is. The parachutes came down,” the announcer continued.

“Crash fire rescue and various other emergency services are on their way to the pilots and crew. There were four good parachutes,” the announcer said in a later statement.

“That is always a positive in our world. If you are so inclined to take the time now to say a prayer,” the announcer concluded.

Dramatic video shows the two fighter jets colliding in midair before four parachutes are deployed.

Both aircraft appeared to be flying extremely close together when they collided and seemingly became entangled, hurtling toward the ground as sparks shot off.

The two jets, which appear to be Navy Super Hornet fighters, smashed into the runway with an enormous bang, producing a huge fireball and a cloud of smoke.

Organizers, the Mountain Home Gunfighters, confirmed that the base was on lockdown in a statement posted on social media.

This was the first time the air show had been held in eight years, after the last event in 2018 saw a hang glider pilot die in an accident, reported the Idaho Stateman.

In 2003, a pilot in the Thunderbirds squadron was forced to eject after his plane crashed during the event.

BREAKING: Two U.S. Navy jets collided mid-air and exploded during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show at Mountain Home Air Force Base. pic.twitter.com/R66ADWM2TY

The base did not respond immediately to requests for comment.

This is a breaking story. Please check back for updates.

---

[Lähde: FOX 7 Austin]
A show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho was called off on May 17 after two fighter jets collided, the base said in a statement on Facebook. (Steven S Ogden via Storyful)

MOUNTAIN HOME, Idaho - Four crew members safely ejected after two Navy jets collided during an air show in Idaho on Sunday, according to an event organizer.

Emergency crews responded after the two planes collided during the show at a military base in western Idaho.

All four of the crew members from the planes ejected safely, said Kim Sykes, marketing director with Silver Wings of Idaho, which helped to plan the air show. Sykes said the crash occurred off base and she did not see the crash but saw the smoke afterward.

The Mountain Home Air Force Base said in a social media post that it was locked down following the incident during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show. Responders were on the scene and an investigation was underway.

Four crew members safely ejected after two Navy jets collided during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in western Idaho on Sunday. (Steven S Ogden via Storyful)

No other information was immediately available, said a person who answered the phone at the 366th Fighter Wing public affairs office.

Multiple witnesses reported two planes collided and crashed, and videos posted online showed four parachutes opening in the sky as the aircraft plummet to the ground near the base about 50 miles (80 kilometers) south of Boise.

Organizers said the popular air show that includes flying demonstrations and parachute jumps is a celebration of aviation history and a look at modern military capabilities. The U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds headlined the show both days.

The National Weather Service reported good visibility and winds gusting up to 29 mph (47 kph) around the time of the crash.

The Source: The Associated Press contributed to this report. Information in the story came from statements by Kim Sykes, marketing director for Silver Wings of Idaho, witness accounts and videos posted online showing parachutes opening after the collision, and social media updates from Mountain Home Air Force Base. This story was reported from Los Angeles.

---

[Lähde: ABC (Australian Broadcasting Corporation)]
The two Growlers collided in mid-air, prompting the crew to bail out over Mountain Home Air Force Base. (US Navy: Petty Officer 3rd class Nathan Burke)

payload.title: Laivaston koneet törmäsivät lentonäytöksessä Idahossa, neljä miehistön jäsentä pelastui
payload.summary: Kaksi Yhdysvaltain laivaston EA-18G-konetta törmäsi ilmassa Gunfighter Skies -lentonäytöksessä Idahossa. Neljä miehistön jäsentä poistui koneista heittoistuimilla, ja tukikohdan mukaan he ovat vakaassa tilassa.
payload.content:
Kaksi Yhdysvaltain laivaston EA-18G-konetta törmäsi ilmassa sunnuntaina Gunfighter Skies -lentonäytöksen aikana Idahossa. Kaikki neljä koneissa ollutta miehistön jäsentä poistui koneista heittoistuimilla, ja Mountain Home Air Force Basen mukaan he ovat onnettomuuden jälkeen vakaassa tilassa.

## Näytös peruttiin törmäyksen jälkeen

Onnettomuus tapahtui lentonäytöksen toisena ja viimeisenä päivänä Mountain Home Air Force Basen lähistöllä Länsi-Idahossa. BBC:n mukaan tapahtumapaikka oli noin kahden mailin eli 3,2 kilometrin päässä tukikohdasta luoteeseen. FOX 7 Austinin välittämien tietojen mukaan tukikohta sijaitsee noin 50 mailia eli 80 kilometriä Boisen eteläpuolella.

Koneet olivat mukana ilmademonstraatiossa, kun ne törmäsivät ja putosivat. Useat silminnäkijät kertoivat kahden koneen osuneen toisiinsa ja syöksyneen maahan. Verkossa julkaistuilla videoilla näkyi neljän laskuvarjon avautuvan taivaalla samalla, kun ilma-alukset putosivat tukikohdan lähellä.

Lentonäytöksen loppu peruttiin onnettomuuden jälkeen. Tukikohta kertoi sosiaalisessa mediassa, että alue suljettiin hetkellisesti tapahtuman jälkeen. Paikalle lähetettiin pelastushenkilöstöä, ja törmäyksen jälkeen alueella syttyi myös tulipalo.

## Miehistö vakaassa tilassa

Yhdysvaltain laivaston tiedottaja kertoi CBS Newsille, että kaikki mukana olleet miehistön jäsenet pääsivät poistumaan koneista turvallisesti. Viranomaiset eivät kuitenkaan heti kertoneet, olivatko he loukkaantuneet. Mountain Home Air Force Base Gunfighters ilmoitti sunnuntaina sosiaalisessa mediassa, että onnettomuudessa mukana ollut miehistö oli vakaassa tilassa.

Lentonäytöksen järjestelyissä mukana olleen Silver Wings of Idahon markkinointijohtaja Kim Sykes sanoi, että kaikki neljä miehistön jäsentä pääsivät ulos koneista turvallisesti. Hänen mukaansa törmäys tapahtui tukikohdan ulkopuolella. Sykes kertoi, ettei nähnyt itse törmäystä, mutta näki savun sen jälkeen.

Onnettomuuden syytä ei kerrottu heti. Tukikohdan mukaan tutkinta on käynnissä, eikä 366th Fighter Wingin julkisuustoimistosta annettu tapahtuman jälkeen välittömästi muuta lisätietoa.
summary_bullets: Kaksi Yhdysvaltain laivaston EA-18G-konetta törmäsi ilmassa Idahon Gunfighter Skies -lentonäytöksessä.
Neljä miehistön jäsentä poistui koneista heittoistuimilla ja on tukikohdan mukaan vakaassa tilassa.
Lentonäytöksen loppu peruttiin, tukikohta suljettiin hetkellisesti ja onnettomuuden tutkinta on käynnissä.
payload.journalist_note: Korjaus perustuu packetin lähteisiin: kaksi Navy EA-18G -konetta, neljä miehistön jäsentä, turvallinen poistuminen, vakaa tila, Gunfighter Skies / Mountain Home Air Force Base, hetkellinen sulku, pelastushenkilöstö, tulipalo ja käynnissä oleva tutkinta. Loukkaantumisia, syytä tai maavahinkoja ei väitetä varmoina.
